literal: Even inside the folded hands (of worship), a weapon will be hidden; the wept tears of enemies are also like that.
translation: A weapon may lie hidden even within the clasped hands of worshipping foes; the tears they weep are of the very same deceptive nature.
modern: பகைவர்கள் வணங்கித் தொழும் கைகளின் உள்ளேயும் கொலைக்கருவி மறைந்திருக்கும்; அவர்கள் அழுது சிந்தும கண்ணீரும் அத்தகையதே (வஞ்சனை உடையதே).
explanation: This couplet warns us to be extremely cautious of the outward displays of submission or grief shown by our adversaries. The poet uses the powerful image of hands folded in worship (தொழுதகை) to show how gestures of respect can literally hide a weapon (படை) meant for our destruction. In the same manner, the tears (கண்ணீர்) shed by an enemy are not signs of genuine remorse or sorrow, but are equally deceptive tools used to disarm our vigilance. We must look past these superficial behaviors to protect ourselves from hidden hostility.
